description: Calculate Pancheros calories, protein, carbs and fat. Free Pancheros nutrition calculator with complete menu data for all items.
articleHtml:
Pancheros builds a burrito differently from most fast-casual Mexican chains.

The restaurant makes its flour tortillas from dough in-house, presses them fresh to order, fills them with the ingredients you choose, and then mixes those fillings before rolling the burrito. Pancheros calls this its “perfectly mixed” approach.

From a nutrition perspective, however, the calculation is still easiest when you separate that perfectly mixed burrito back into its individual parts.

Use the Pancheros Nutrition Calculator above to choose your entrée, tortilla or base, rice, beans, protein, cheese, queso, guacamole, vegetables, salsa, dressing, and sides.

The Fresh-Pressed Tortilla Is a Major Part of the Burrito

Pancheros makes its tortillas in-house rather than using a small prepackaged wrap.

The nutrition sheet currently linked from the official Pancheros menu lists approximately:

Large Tortilla: 350 calories

Small Tortilla: 80 calories.

That makes the large tortilla one of the biggest single calorie contributors in a standard burrito before rice, beans, meat, cheese, or queso are added.

This is why a Burrito and Burrito Bowl should not automatically share the same nutrition total.

A Burrito Should Be Built From the Inside Out

A Pancheros burrito can contain:

Fresh-pressed tortilla

Cilantro Lime Rice

Black or Pinto Beans

Chicken, Steak, Carnitas, or plant-based protein

Cheese

Queso

Guacamole

Sautéed vegetables

Salsa

Sour cream

Jalapeños

and other available toppings. The current menu explicitly presents these ingredients as customizable components.

For the most useful estimate, add only the ingredients that are actually in your burrito.

The Bowl Removes the Tortilla, Not the Rest of the Burrito

Pancheros describes its Burrito Bowl as everything you enjoy in a burrito without the tortilla. Current bowls can still contain rice, beans, protein, cheese, salsa, and other toppings.

That means a bowl is not automatically a low-calorie meal.

Removing the large tortilla can make a substantial difference, but the final result still depends on:

Rice portion

Protein

Cheese or queso

Guacamole

Sour cream

Salsa

and other additions.

Calculate the actual bowl rather than taking one generic burrito value and subtracting an estimated amount.

Rice Adds More Than a Small Garnish

The nutrition PDF currently linked by Pancheros lists one standard Cilantro Lime Rice portion at approximately:

210 calories

39g carbohydrates

4g protein

800mg sodium .

This makes rice a substantial part of the meal, especially when combined with the tortilla in a burrito.

If you skip rice, remove it from the build rather than leaving it in a standard burrito estimate.

Black and Pinto Beans Need Separate Entries

Pancheros currently offers both:

Black Beans

and

Pinto Beans .

The linked nutrition sheet lists a serving of each at about 60 calories, but their carbohydrate, fiber, and protein values are not identical.

Select the bean you actually order.

If you skip beans, do not automatically include them simply because they appear in a typical burrito recipe.

Protein Choice Changes the Meal Quickly

Pancheros' live menu currently highlights:

Chicken

Steak

Carnitas

and its plant-based option, currently labeled Tofurizo on the live menu.

The nutrition document currently linked from that menu gives larger serving examples of approximately:

Chicken, 2.8 oz: 80 calories and 10g protein

Steak, 2.8 oz: 110 calories and 20g protein

Carnitas, 4 oz: 170 calories and 24g protein.

These serving sizes are different, so protein should be compared using the published restaurant portion rather than equal-ounce assumptions.

Steak and Chicken Have Very Different Sodium Profiles

The currently linked nutrition sheet lists the larger Steak serving at approximately:

660mg sodium

while Chicken is approximately:

390mg sodium .

Calories therefore tell only part of the story.

When comparing proteins, look at:

Calories

Protein

Fat

Sodium

together.

Pancheros Has a Naming Problem Around Its Plant-Based Protein

This deserves special attention.

The current live menu calls the plant-based protein “Tofurizo.”

However, Pancheros' linked nutrition PDF and allergen information still use the older name Tofusada® .

NutritionSolver should not show these as two unrelated proteins unless Pancheros confirms that they are genuinely different recipes.

A cleaner current label would be:

Tofurizo, previously listed as Tofusada in Pancheros nutrition materials

until the company updates or clarifies the official documentation.

Queso Can Be One of the Largest Additions

Queso is much more than a small salsa topping.

Pancheros' currently linked nutrition sheet provides two serving contexts:

Queso, 1.9 oz: about 190 calories

Queso, 5 oz: about 390 calories.

The larger serving also contains approximately 31g fat and 1,480mg sodium .

This makes portion labeling essential.

A little queso added inside a burrito and a large side of queso should never receive the same nutrition value.

Guacamole Also Needs the Correct Portion

Pancheros publishes different guacamole portions as well.

Its linked nutrition sheet lists approximately:

Guacamole, 2.1 oz: 70 calories

Guacamole, 5.5 oz: 190 calories.

The smaller portion makes sense as an entrée addition, while the larger serving can represent a much more substantial side.

NutritionSolver should display the portion beside the ingredient name.

Shredded Cheese Can Add More Than Expected

The official nutrition sheet currently linked by Pancheros lists:

Shredded Cheese, 0.6 oz: about 70 calories

and a much larger:

2.3 oz serving: about 260 calories.

Once again, context matters.

A cheese serving used inside an entrée should not automatically be replaced by a large side or catering-style portion.

Salsa Should Be Selected by Recipe and Portion

Pancheros' current menu includes several homemade salsas:

Mild Ancho Salsa

Medium Salsa Verde

Hot Tomatillo Salsa

Roasted Corn Salsa

Pico de Gallo .

These are not nutritionally identical.

The linked nutrition sheet also publishes different small and large serving amounts for several of them.

For example, Roasted Corn Salsa is listed at approximately:

70 calories for 1.62 oz

and:

180 calories for 4.22 oz .

Use the actual portion context instead of one universal salsa figure.

Salsa Heat Does Not Tell You the Calories

The current menu labels Mild Ancho, Salsa Verde, Hot Tomatillo, Roasted Corn, and Pico de Gallo with different heat levels.

Spicier does not automatically mean higher in calories.

For example, the linked nutrition data places many salsa servings quite low in calories, while a corn-based salsa can contribute more.

Choose salsa by its actual recipe and serving rather than its heat level.

Chile Lime Vinaigrette Makes the Salad a Different Meal

Pancheros' current Salad is served on lettuce with protein, beans, cheese, salsa, and its Chile Lime Vinaigrette.

The linked nutrition sheet lists the vinaigrette at approximately:

110 calories

11g fat

12g carbohydrates

135mg sodium .

That means the dressing should not disappear from a salad calculation.

If you use the standard dressing, include it.

If you skip or replace it, calculate the meal accordingly.

A Pancheros Salad Is Not Simply Lettuce and Chicken

The salad format can contain:

Lettuce

Protein

Black or Pinto Beans

Cheese

Salsa

Chile Lime Vinaigrette

plus other customizations.

The lettuce base itself contributes very little, but the cheese, protein, beans, guac, queso, and dressing can contribute much more.

Build the complete salad rather than drawing conclusions from the greens alone.

Tacos Use Two Fresh-Pressed Tortillas

Pancheros currently serves its taco entrée as two tacos on fresh-pressed soft flour tortillas with the customer's selected protein, lettuce, cheese, and salsa.

That serving structure should be visible in the calculator.

Use:

Tacos, 2 count

then add:

protein + cheese + salsa + toppings

rather than calculating a single taco and assuming it represents the entire menu order.

Quesadilla Is a Cheese-Forward Build

Pancheros describes its Quesadilla as a large fresh-grilled flour tortilla filled with cheese and the customer's selected protein, with salsa on the side.

That makes the quesadilla fundamentally different from a burrito.

It starts with:

Tortilla + cheese + protein

rather than tortilla, rice, beans, and multiple toppings by default.

Use its own build logic.

The Kidsadilla Is a Real Published Serving

Pancheros' Kids Menu currently includes:

Kidsadilla

Single Taco

Side of Rice

and is available in-restaurant.

The linked nutrition sheet lists the Kidsadilla at approximately:

410 calories

21g protein

27g carbohydrates

25g fat

700mg sodium .

That is a complete Kidsadilla record, so it should not be confused with the calories of a small tortilla alone.

Blue Corn Chips Can Add 450 Calories Before the Dip

Pancheros currently promotes blue corn chips with queso, salsa, or guacamole.

The linked nutrition sheet lists the standard chips serving at approximately:

450 calories

61g carbohydrates

22g fat

350mg sodium .

Then the dip is another component.

That makes:

Burrito only

very different from:

Burrito + chips + 5 oz queso .

Always add sides when you actually eat them.

Queso, Guac, and Salsa Dips Should Stay Separate

The current menu specifically promotes chips with:

Queso

Homemade salsa

Fresh-made guacamole .

A chips-and-dip calculator should therefore work as:

Chips → choose dip → choose dip serving

rather than assigning every order the same total.

This is especially important because the published queso and guacamole servings vary widely in size.

“Perfectly Mixed” Does Not Change the Nutrition Total

Pancheros uses its proprietary mixing tool to distribute the ingredients through a burrito before rolling it.

Mixing changes how the ingredients are distributed across each bite.

It does not mean you should count the ingredients differently.

The nutrition total is still the sum of the tortilla, rice, beans, protein, cheese, salsa, and other selected components.

Pancheros Nutrition Questions

How many calories are in a Pancheros burrito?+
How many calories are in a Pancheros tortilla?+
Is a Pancheros bowl lower in calories than a burrito?+
How many calories are in Pancheros queso?+
How many calories are in Pancheros chips?+
Does Pancheros have a plant-based protein?+
Does Pancheros have a salad?+

Build the Pancheros Order Before You Add It Up

Start by choosing the correct Burrito, Bowl, two Tacos, Quesadilla, or Salad .

Then select the exact tortilla or base, Cilantro Lime Rice, Black or Pinto Beans, protein, cheese, queso, guacamole, vegetables, salsa, dressing, and other toppings .

After the entrée is complete, add any blue corn chips, side queso, guacamole, extra salsa, beverage, or Kids Menu item that is actually part of the order.

Pancheros may mix all the ingredients together before rolling the burrito, but NutritionSolver should keep those components separate behind the scenes so the final nutrition total remains transparent.

faqs.q: How many calories are in a Pancheros burrito?
faqs.a:
There is no single value for every burrito because Pancheros lets you select the protein, beans, cheese, salsa, queso, guacamole, and other ingredients. The large tortilla alone is listed at approximately
    

     350 calories
    

     in the nutrition sheet currently linked by Pancheros.

faqs.q: How many calories are in a Pancheros tortilla?
faqs.a:
The currently linked nutrition information lists approximately
    

     350 calories for the Large Tortilla
    

     and
    

     80 calories for the Small Tortilla
    

     .

faqs.q: Is a Pancheros bowl lower in calories than a burrito?
faqs.a: A bowl removes the flour tortilla, but its final nutrition still depends on rice, beans, protein, cheese, queso, guacamole, salsa, and other toppings.

faqs.q: How many calories are in Pancheros queso?
faqs.a:
The currently linked nutrition sheet lists approximately
    

     190 calories for a 1.9 oz serving
    

     and
    

     390 calories for a 5 oz serving
    

     .

faqs.q: How many calories are in Pancheros chips?
faqs.a:
The official nutrition sheet currently linked from the menu lists one 3.2 oz chips serving at approximately
    

     450 calories
    

     .

faqs.q: Does Pancheros have a plant-based protein?
faqs.a:
Yes. The current live menu labels its plant-based protein
    

     Tofurizo
    

     , although older linked nutrition and allergen documents still use the Tofusada name.
Yes. The current salad uses lettuce with selected protein, beans, cheese, salsa, and Chile Lime Vinaigrette.
